source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς λόγους τούτους, μετῆρεν ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια τῆς Ἰουδαίας πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.

records.literal_gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus the words these, he moved away from the Galilee and came into the regions of the Judea beyond the Jordan.

en.L: And it happened, when Jesus had finished these words, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved on from Galilee and came into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.
en.B: When Jesus had finished saying these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left Galilee and went on into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.
en.R: When Jesus finished saying these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left Galilee. He went south to the land of Judea and to the area on the east side of the Jordan River.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Jesús terminó estas palabras, se marchó de Galilea y fue a la región de Judea al otro lado del Jordán.
es.B: Cuando Jesús terminó de decir estas cosas, salió de Galilea y se fue a la región de Judea, al otro lado del Jordán.
es.R: Cuando Jesús terminó de decir estas cosas, salió de Galilea. Se fue al sur, a la tierra de Judea y a la zona que está al este del río Jordán.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand Jésus eut achevé ces paroles, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} quitta la Galilée et vint dans le territoire de la Judée, au-delà du Jourdain.
fr.B: Lorsque Jésus eut fini de prononcer ces paroles, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} quitta la Galilée et se rendit dans la région de la Judée, au-delà du Jourdain.
fr.R: Quand Jésus a fini de dire tout cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a quitté la Galilée. Il est descendu vers le sud, dans la région de la Judée et dans la région qui se trouve à l’est du fleuve Jourdain.

sw.L: Na ikawa, Yesu alipomaliza maneno haya, alihama kutoka Galilaya, akaja katika maeneo ya Uyahudi ng'ambo ya Yordani.
sw.B: Yesu alipomaliza kusema hayo, aliondoka Galilaya, akaenda mpaka eneo la Uyahudi, ng'ambo ya Yordani.
sw.R: Yesu alipomaliza kusema mambo hayo, aliondoka Galilaya. Akaenda kusini mpaka nchi ya Uyahudi, na eneo lililo mashariki mwa Mto Yordani.

vi.L: Và xảy ra là, khi Đức Giê-xu đã nói xong những lời này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời khỏi Ga-li-lê và đến miền Giu-đê, bên kia [sông] Giô-đanh.
vi.B: Khi Đức Giê-xu nói xong những điều ấy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời Ga-li-lê và đến miền Giu-đê, bên kia sông Giô-đanh.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu nói xong những điều ấy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời miền Ga-li-lê. Ngài đi về phía nam, đến miền Giu-đê và vùng phía đông sông Giô-đanh.

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 이 말씀들을 마치셨을 때에 [이런 일이 있었다]. 그분이 갈릴리에서 떠나 요단 건너편 유대 지역으로 가셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 이 말씀들을 다 마치시고, 갈릴리를 떠나 요단 강 건너편 유대 지방으로 가셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 이 말씀들을 다 하시고 나서 갈릴리를 떠나셨다. 그리고 남쪽으로 내려가 유대 지방과 요단 강 동쪽 지역으로 가셨다.

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished these words: the formula that closes the fourth long speech
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech with these words (7:28; 11:1; 13:53; 26:1). This one closes the teaching of chapter 18.

decisions.choice: the region of Judea beyond the Jordan: Judea, and the land east of the river through which Jesus traveled to reach it
alternatives: a part of Judea lying east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Judea itself lay west of the Jordan. The phrase most likely joins the two areas Jesus now works in; Mark 10:1 says "Judea and beyond the Jordan". Travelers from Galilee often went south on the east side of the river.

decisions.choice: went south to the land of Judea and to the area on the east side of the Jordan River
alternatives: came into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan
decisions.reason: Readable names both areas and says where they lie.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (él, lo, le, su, mí, mi)
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("salió", "se fue") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("ponerlo"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English, as in Mark 16. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("disent", 19:7, 19:10)
decisions.reason: As in Mark and Luke: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives
decisions.reason: As in John and the rest of Matthew: Swahili marks "he" and "him" inside the verb ("aliondoka", "walimfuata"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("naye", "yake", "kwangu"). Swahili has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "Và xảy ra là" (L)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 11:1 and 13:53: Literal keeps the formula that closes each of Jesus's long discourses.

decisions.choice: "마치셨을 때에" kept as the closing formula of the speech, with [이런 일이 있었다] at Literal; no deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 19:1-15
decisions.reason: Matthew's formula that closes the fourth long speech (meaning decision), worded as in the Korean Matthew 11:1. Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시- (style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "요단 건너편" (L); "요단 강 건너편" (B); "요단 강 동쪽 지역" (R)
decisions.reason: The Protestant form of the name (style guide, section 5), as in the Korean Matthew 4:15 and Mark 10:1; Readable says where the land lay, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς ἐκεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And followed him crowds many, and he healed them there.

en.L: And large crowds followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them there.
en.B: Great crowds went after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.
en.R: Large crowds of people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed the sick people there.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron grandes multitudes, y los sanó allí.
es.B: Grandes multitudes {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron, y allí los sanó.
es.R: Muchísima gente {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió, y allí sanó a los enfermos.

fr.L: Et de grandes foules {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les guérit là.
fr.B: Des foules nombreuses {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent, et là {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les guérit.
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont suivi, et là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a guéri les malades.

sw.L: Na makutano mengi walimfuata, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawaponya huko.
sw.B: Umati mkubwa wa watu ulimfuata, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawaponya huko.
sw.R: Makundi makubwa ya watu yalimfuata, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawaponya wagonjwa waliokuwa huko.

vi.L: Và đoàn dân đông đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa lành họ tại đó.
vi.B: Dân chúng kéo đến rất đông đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa lành cho họ tại đó.
vi.R: Rất nhiều người đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa lành cho những người bệnh ở đó.

ko.L: 그리고 많은 무리가 그분을 따랐고, 그분은 거기에서 그들을 고쳐 주셨다.
ko.B: 많은 무리가 예수를 따라왔고, 예수께서는 거기에서 그들을 고쳐 주셨다.
ko.R: 많은 사람이 예수를 따라왔다. 예수께서는 거기에서 아픈 사람들을 고쳐 주셨다.

decisions.choice: he healed them: he healed the sick among the crowds
alternatives: every person in the crowds was ill
decisions.reason: As in 12:15 and 15:30, "them" means those in the crowds who needed healing.

decisions.choice: the sick people
decisions.reason: Readable says whom Jesus healed.

source.text: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Φαρισαῖοι πειράζοντες αὐτὸν καὶ λέγοντες· Εἰ ἔξεστιν ἀνθρώπῳ ἀπολῦσαι τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ κατὰ πᾶσαν αἰτίαν;

records.literal_gloss: And came to him Pharisees testing him and saying, If it is lawful for a man to divorce the wife of him for every cause?

en.L: And Pharisees came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and saying, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?"
en.B: Some Pharisees came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the test. "Does the law allow a man to divorce his wife for any reason at all?" they asked.
en.R: Some Pharisees came to Jesus. They wanted to trap {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with a hard question. So they asked, "Does God's law let a man divorce his wife for any reason he wants?"

es.L: Y vinieron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} fariseos, que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ponían a prueba y decían: «¿Es lícito a un hombre divorciarse de su mujer por cualquier motivo?».
es.B: Unos fariseos se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para ponerlo a prueba. «¿Permite la ley que un hombre se divorcie de su mujer por cualquier motivo?», le preguntaron.
es.R: Unos fariseos fueron a ver a Jesús. Querían tenderle una trampa con una pregunta difícil. Así que le preguntaron: «¿Deja la ley de Dios que un hombre se divorcie de su esposa por cualquier razón que quiera?».

fr.L: Et des Pharisiens s’approchèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettant à l’épreuve et disant : « Est-il permis à un homme de renvoyer sa femme pour n’importe quel motif ? »
fr.B: Des Pharisiens vinrent {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trouver pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettre à l’épreuve. « La Loi permet-elle à un homme de divorcer d’avec sa femme pour n’importe quelle raison ? » demandèrent-ils.
fr.R: Des Pharisiens sont venus voir Jésus. Ils voulaient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} piéger avec une question difficile. Alors ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé : « Est-ce que la Loi de Dieu permet à un homme de divorcer d’avec sa femme pour la raison qu’il veut ? »

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo walimjia, wakimjaribu na kusema, "Je, ni halali mtu kumtaliki mke wake kwa kila sababu?"
sw.B: Mafarisayo kadhaa walimjia ili wamjaribu. Wakamwuliza, "Je, sheria inamruhusu mtu kumtaliki mke wake kwa sababu yoyote ile?"
sw.R: Baadhi ya Mafarisayo walimjia Yesu. Walitaka kumtega kwa swali gumu. Basi wakamwuliza, "Je, sheria ya Mungu inamruhusu mwanamume kumtaliki mkewe kwa sababu yoyote anayotaka?"

vi.L: Và [mấy] người Pha-ri-si đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để thử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Người ta có được phép ly dị vợ mình vì bất cứ lý do nào không?"
vi.B: Có mấy người Pha-ri-si đến để thử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ hỏi: "Luật pháp có cho phép một người đàn ông ly dị vợ mình vì bất cứ lý do gì không?"
vi.R: Có mấy người Pha-ri-si đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Họ muốn gài bẫy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bằng một câu hỏi khó. Họ hỏi: "Luật pháp của Đức Chúa Trời có cho phép một người đàn ông ly dị vợ mình vì bất cứ lý do nào ông ta muốn không?"

ko.L: 그리고 바리새파 사람들이 그분께 와서, 그분을 시험하며 말했다. "사람이 아무 이유로나 자기 아내와 이혼하는 것이 옳습니까?"
ko.B: 바리새파 사람 몇이 예수를 시험하려고 와서 물었다. "남자가 무슨 이유로든 아내와 이혼하는 것이 율법에 맞습니까?"
ko.R: 바리새파 사람 몇이 예수께 왔다. 그들은 어려운 질문으로 예수를 곤란하게 만들려고 했다. 그래서 물었다. "남자가 마음에 드는 이유만 있으면 아내와 이혼해도 하나님의 율법이 허락합니까?"

decisions.choice: testing him: trying to catch him out
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the Pharisees in 16:1 and 22:35. Any answer would set Jesus against one party or another.

decisions.choice: for any cause: the debate over the grounds for divorce in Deuteronomy 24:1
alternatives: a general question whether divorce is ever right
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a husband finding "something indecent" in his wife. Jewish teachers disagreed about what that meant: the school of Shammai allowed divorce only for unfaithfulness, the school of Hillel for almost any cause (Mishnah Gittin 9:10). See 5:31-32.

decisions.choice: a man divorcing his wife: in Jewish law only the husband could divorce
decisions.reason: As at 5:31, the question is put from the husband's side, because only he had the right to end the marriage.

decisions.choice: the test may also have had a political edge
alternatives: a question about the law only
decisions.reason: Jesus was now in the territory of Herod Antipas, who had put John the Baptist in prison for condemning his marriage (14:3-4). Matthew does not say this was part of the trap.

decisions.choice: Does the law allow (B); Does God's law let (R)
decisions.reason: "Lawful" means allowed by the law of Moses; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: divorciarse de (every level)
decisions.reason: The verb means to send a wife away, which in Jewish law was divorce (meaning decision m3). "Divorciarse" says that plainly at every level, as the English "divorce" does; "repudiar" is the older Bible word and now sounds legal and harsh. The same through verse 9.

decisions.choice: renvoyer (L); divorcer d’avec (B, R), here and in 19:7-9
decisions.reason: As Mark 10:2: the Greek verb means "send away", and 19:7 uses it for the man sending his wife away, so Literal keeps "renvoyer" each time. Balanced and Readable say "divorcer", the plain modern word. "Répudier" is exact but now a legal or historical term.

decisions.choice: kumtaliki (every level)
decisions.reason: The verb means to send a wife away, which in Jewish law was divorce (meaning decision m3). "Kutaliki" is the standard word for a husband divorcing his wife and says that at every level, as the English "divorce" does; "kumwacha" (to leave her) is softer and could mean only living apart. The same through verse 9.

decisions.choice: "ly dị" for divorce at every level, through 19:9
decisions.reason: As in Mark 10:2-12 and Matthew 5:31-32; "ly dị" is the ordinary modern word.

decisions.choice: "Người ta" (L) for "a man", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The question is about husbands, which "vợ mình" makes plain; Balanced and Readable say "một người đàn ông".

decisions.choice: "이혼하다" for apolyo at every level, through 19:9
decisions.reason: The Korean Matthew already says "이혼하다" at every level for the same verb in 5:31-32, so Matthew keeps it; the Korean Mark's Literal "버리다" is the alternative.

decisions.choice: The Pharisees speak to Jesus in 합쇼체; "시험하다" for testing
decisions.reason: They come to catch him out (meaning decision) but speak to him correctly, as in the Korean Mark 10:2; "사람" for anthropos takes no gender span (L), and Balanced and Readable say "남자" since only the husband could divorce (meaning decision).

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι ὁ κτίσας ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν· Ἕνεκα τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ κολληθήσεται τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν;

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said, Not did you read that the [one] having created from beginning male and female made them \v 5 and said, On account of this will leave a man the father and the mother and will be joined to the wife of him, and will be the two into flesh one?

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "Have you not read that the one who created [them] from [the] beginning made them male and female, \v 5 and said, 'For this reason a man will leave [his] father and mother and will be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh'?
en.B: Jesus answered, "Have you never read that the Creator, at the beginning, made them male and female? \v 5 And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'That is why a man will leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh.'
en.R: Jesus answered, "Have you not read in the Scriptures what God did in the beginning? He made people male and female. \v 5 And God said, 'That is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife. The two of them will become one, as if they were one body.'

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiendo, dijo: «¿No {{plural_you:han leído|habéis leído}} que el que [los] creó desde [el] principio los hizo varón y hembra, \v 5 y dijo: “Por esto dejará el hombre a [su] padre y a [su] madre, y quedará unido a su mujer, y los dos llegarán a ser una sola carne”?
es.B: Jesús respondió: «¿Nunca {{plural_you:han leído|habéis leído}} que el Creador, al principio, los hizo hombre y mujer? \v 5 Y dijo: “Por eso el hombre dejará a su padre y a su madre, se unirá a su esposa, y los dos serán una sola carne”.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «¿No {{plural_you:han leído|habéis leído}} en las Escrituras lo que Dios hizo al principio? Hizo a las personas hombre y mujer. \v 5 Y Dios dijo: “Por eso el hombre dejará a su padre y a su madre y se unirá a su esposa. Los dos llegarán a ser uno solo, como si fueran un solo cuerpo”.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} répondit et dit : « N’avez-vous pas lu que celui qui [les] a créés dès le commencement les a faits mâle et femelle, \v 5 et a dit : “C’est pourquoi un homme quittera [son] père et [sa] mère et sera uni à sa femme, et les deux deviendront une seule chair” ?
fr.B: Jésus répondit : « N’avez-vous jamais lu qu’au commencement le Créateur les a faits homme et femme ? \v 5 Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : “Voilà pourquoi un homme quittera son père et sa mère pour s’attacher à sa femme, et les deux ne seront qu’une seule chair.”
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « N’avez-vous pas lu dans les Écritures ce que Dieu a fait au commencement ? Il a fait les humains homme et femme. \v 5 Et Dieu a dit : “C’est pour cela qu’un homme quittera son père et sa mère et sera uni à sa femme. Les deux ne feront plus qu’un, comme s’ils n’avaient qu’un seul corps.”

sw.L: Naye akajibu, akasema, "Je, hamjasoma kwamba aliyewaumba tangu mwanzo aliwafanya mwanamume na mwanamke, \v 5 akasema, 'Kwa ajili hiyo mtu atamwacha baba na mama, naye ataungwa na mke wake, na wale wawili watakuwa mwili mmoja'?
sw.B: Yesu alijibu, "Je, hamjawahi kusoma kwamba Muumba, hapo mwanzo, aliwafanya mwanamume na mwanamke? \v 5 Kisha akasema, 'Ndiyo sababu mwanamume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, ashikamane na mke wake, nao wawili watakuwa mwili mmoja.'
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Je, hamjasoma katika Maandiko kile Mungu alichofanya mwanzoni? Aliwaumba watu wakiwa mwanamume na mwanamke. \v 5 Kisha Mungu akasema, 'Ndiyo sababu mwanamume atamwacha baba yake na mama yake, aungane na mke wake. Hao wawili watakuwa kitu kimoja, kana kwamba ni mwili mmoja.'

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời và nói: "Các người chưa đọc sao: Đấng Tạo Hóa từ ban đầu đã làm nên họ có nam có nữ, \v 5 và phán: 'Vì cớ đó, người nam sẽ lìa cha và mẹ mà gắn bó với vợ mình, và hai người sẽ trở nên một thịt'?
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Các người chưa bao giờ đọc thấy rằng lúc ban đầu Đấng Tạo Hóa đã dựng nên con người có nam có nữ sao? \v 5 Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: 'Vì thế, người nam sẽ lìa cha mẹ mà gắn bó với vợ mình, và hai người sẽ trở nên một thân.'
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Các người chưa đọc trong Kinh Thánh về điều Đức Chúa Trời đã làm lúc ban đầu sao? Ngài đã dựng nên con người có nam và có nữ. \v 5 Và Đức Chúa Trời phán: 'Vì thế, người đàn ông sẽ rời cha mẹ để gắn bó với vợ mình. Hai người sẽ trở nên một, như thể họ là một thân thể.'

decisions.choice: male and female he made them: Genesis 1:27

decisions.choice: Genesis 2:24, quoted as the Greek translation of Genesis has it
decisions.reason: "The two" is in the Greek translation of Genesis but not in the Hebrew text, which says "they will become one flesh". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: and said: the Creator is the speaker of Genesis 2:24
decisions.reason: In Genesis the words are the narrator's comment. Jesus treats them as what God himself said, so they carry God's authority.

decisions.choice: the one who created, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the one who made, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts have the more common verb "made". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with "he said" for the Creator
decisions.reason: Balanced breaks the long question in two so the quotation is clear.

decisions.choice: will become one, as if they were one body
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of one flesh.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the Pharisees as a group, so every plural "you" and its verb in his replies (19:4-9) is the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). English has no such choice. The same in verse 14, to the disciples.

decisions.choice: varón y hembra (L); hombre y mujer (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the pair of words of Genesis 1:27 (meaning decision m1), which name the two sexes; Balanced and Readable say it in everyday words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: mâle et femelle (L); homme et femme (B, R)
alternatives: mâle et femelle at every level
decisions.reason: As Mark 10:6: Literal keeps the Greek adjectives of Genesis 1:27; in current French "mâle et femelle" said of people sounds like biology, so Balanced and Readable say "homme et femme".

decisions.choice: "các người" for the Pharisees (19:4-9)
decisions.reason: As settled for Matthew (12:3, 15:3): Jesus speaks to opponents as "các người".

decisions.choice: "một thịt" (L); "một thân" (B); "một, như thể họ là một thân thể" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of the Vietnamese Mark 10:8 at Literal and Balanced; God speaking is "phán".

decisions.choice: "너희는 읽지 못하였느냐?" first (L)
alternatives: the question at the end of 19:5
decisions.reason: Korean puts the main verb last, so a question that holds both Genesis texts would end after the quotation and run across the verse marker; Literal asks first and lets each verse keep its own words.

decisions.choice: "창조하신 분" (L); "창조주" (B); "하나님" (R); Genesis 2:24 worded as in the Korean Mark 10:7-8
decisions.reason: The Creator is the speaker of Genesis 2:24 (meaning decision), so the honorific "말씀하셨다" is used for him; the quotation is the same Greek as Mark's and reads alike.

decisions.choice: one flesh: one life and one household, joined in body and in every part of life
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means the whole person. Husband and wife become a new unit, as close as one body, which is why Jesus goes on to forbid parting them.

decisions.choice: a husband and wife
decisions.reason: Readable says who "they" are.

decisions.choice: joined together: yoked together, as a pair
decisions.reason: The verb pictures two animals under one yoke. God is the one who joins husband and wife.

decisions.choice: let not a human being separate: a command, aimed first at the husband who would divorce
alternatives: a statement that divorce is impossible
decisions.reason: "Human being" stands against "God". The verb forbids people to undo what God has done; it does not say that a marriage cannot be broken.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a human being|man}}
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, set against God, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: yoked together
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture in the verb.

decisions.choice: {{gender:un ser humano|el hombre}}
decisions.reason: As the English Literal: the Greek word means a human being, and Spanish can say it either way. The command is aimed first at the husband (meaning decision m2), but it binds anyone; Balanced says "ningún ser humano" and Readable "nadie", which need no span.

decisions.choice: amewafunga nira moja (has yoked them together)
decisions.reason: As the English Balanced "yoked together": the verb pictures two animals under one yoke (meaning decision m1), and "nira" is the Swahili yoke. Literal and Readable say "joined".

decisions.choice: "loài người" (L, B), "không ai" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 10:9, of which this is the parallel; the Vietnamese words are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: "한 멍에로 함께 매어 주다" (L); "하나로 묶어 주다" (B); "하나로 맺어 주다" (R); "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The same Greek as Mark 10:9, worded as the Korean Mark: the verb is to yoke together (meaning decision). "사람" already means any human being, so the English span has nothing to change.

source.text: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Τί οὖν Μωϋσῆς ἐνετείλατο δοῦναι βιβλίον ἀποστασίου καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν;

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 24:1-4: the written notice of divorce

decisions.reason: The question makes Moses' rule sound like an order. Jesus answers that Moses only permitted divorce.

decisions.choice: written notice of divorce (B); a paper saying that she is divorced (R)

decisions.choice: hardness of heart: a stubborn refusal to do God's will
alternatives: hard feelings between husband and wife
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls the prophets' charge against Israel (Deuteronomy 10:16; Jeremiah 4:4). The rule about divorce allowed for human sin; it did not show what God wants.

decisions.choice: your: Jesus includes his hearers with Israel in Moses' day
decisions.reason: The same hardness that made the law necessary is still present in those who ask.

decisions.choice: from the beginning it has not been so: God's purpose at creation never included divorce
alternatives: divorce did not exist until Moses
decisions.reason: The perfect tense looks at the state of things as God made them and as they still should be. Jesus appeals to creation (19:4-6) over the later rule.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: that is not what God planned when he first made people
alternatives: from the beginning it has not been so
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the beginning" refers to.

decisions.choice: "마음의 완고함" (L); "마음이 굳어 있다" (B); "고집이 세다" (R); "허락하다" against the Pharisees' "명령하다"
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 10:5. Jesus corrects their "commanded" to "allowed" (meaning decision); Korean keeps the two verbs distinct at every level.

source.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν ἀπολύσῃ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ μὴ ἐπὶ πορνείᾳ καὶ γαμήσῃ ἄλλην μοιχᾶται καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην γαμήσας μοιχᾶται.

records.literal_gloss: I say but to you that whoever divorces the wife of him not for sexual immorality and marries another commits adultery, and the [one] a divorced [woman] having married commits adultery.

en.L: But I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
en.B: And I tell you this: a man who divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual unfaithfulness and then marries someone else commits adultery, and the man who marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
en.R: But I tell you, if a man divorces his wife for any reason except sexual unfaithfulness, and then he marries another woman, he is guilty of adultery. And a man who marries a divorced woman is guilty of adultery too."

es.L: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que el que se divorcia de su mujer, no por inmoralidad sexual, y se casa con otra, comete adulterio; y el que se casa con una divorciada comete adulterio».
es.B: Y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo esto: el hombre que se divorcia de su mujer por cualquier motivo que no sea la infidelidad sexual, y luego se casa con otra, comete adulterio; y el que se casa con una mujer divorciada comete adulterio».
es.R: Pero yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que si un hombre se divorcia de su esposa por cualquier razón que no sea la infidelidad sexual, y después se casa con otra mujer, es culpable de adulterio. Y el hombre que se casa con una mujer divorciada también es culpable de adulterio».

fr.L: Mais je vous dis que celui qui renvoie sa femme, sauf pour immoralité sexuelle, et en épouse une autre commet un adultère, et celui qui épouse une [femme] renvoyée commet un adultère. »
fr.B: Et moi, je vous le dis : un homme qui divorce d’avec sa femme pour une autre raison que l’infidélité sexuelle et qui en épouse une autre commet un adultère, et celui qui épouse une femme divorcée commet un adultère. »
fr.R: Mais je vous le dis : si un homme divorce d’avec sa femme pour une autre raison que l’infidélité sexuelle, et qu’il épouse une autre femme, il est coupable d’adultère. Et un homme qui épouse une femme divorcée est aussi coupable d’adultère. »

sw.L: Lakini nawaambia kwamba yeyote atakayemtaliki mke wake, isipokuwa kwa sababu ya uasherati, na kuoa mwingine, anazini; na yeye amwoaye aliyetalikiwa anazini."
sw.B: Nami nawaambia hivi: mwanamume anayemtaliki mke wake kwa sababu yoyote isipokuwa uasherati, kisha akaoa mwanamke mwingine, anazini; na mwanamume anayemwoa mwanamke aliyetalikiwa anazini."
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nawaambia, mwanamume akimtaliki mkewe kwa sababu yoyote isipokuwa kukosa uaminifu katika ndoa, kisha akaoa mwanamke mwingine, ana hatia ya uzinzi. Na mwanamume anayemwoa mwanamke aliyetalikiwa naye ana hatia ya uzinzi."

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người rằng ai ly dị vợ mình, không phải vì gian dâm, mà cưới người khác thì phạm tội ngoại tình; và ai cưới người đàn bà đã bị ly dị cũng phạm tội ngoại tình."
vi.B: Ta nói với các người: người nào ly dị vợ mình mà không phải vì vợ đã không chung thủy, rồi cưới người khác, là phạm tội ngoại tình; và người nào cưới người phụ nữ đã bị ly dị cũng phạm tội ngoại tình."
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người: nếu một người đàn ông ly dị vợ mình vì bất cứ lý do nào khác ngoài việc vợ không chung thủy, rồi cưới người phụ nữ khác, thì người ấy phạm tội ngoại tình. Và người đàn ông nào cưới một người phụ nữ đã bị ly dị cũng phạm tội ngoại tình."

ko.L: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 누구든지 음행의 이유 말고 자기 아내와 이혼하고 다른 여자와 결혼하는 사람은 간음하는 것이다. 그리고 이혼당한 여자와 결혼하는 사람도 간음하는 것이다."
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 말한다. 아내가 성적으로 부정을 저지른 경우가 아닌데도 아내와 이혼하고 다른 여자와 결혼하는 사람은 간음하는 것이다. 또 이혼당한 여자와 결혼하는 사람도 간음하는 것이다."
ko.R: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 아내가 다른 남자와 성관계를 한 것이 아닌데도 아내와 이혼하고 다른 여자와 결혼하는 남자는 간음죄를 짓는 것이다. 그리고 이혼당한 여자와 결혼하는 남자도 간음죄를 짓는 것이다."

decisions.choice: sexual immorality: sexual unfaithfulness by the wife
decisions.reason: As at 5:32, the word covers sexual sin of many kinds, and in a saying about marriage it most likely means the wife's unfaithfulness. Others limit it to marriages the law forbade (Leviticus 18) or to unfaithfulness during betrothal (as in 1:19).

decisions.choice: the wording of the SBLGNT, with the closing words about marrying a divorced woman
alternatives: except on account of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery, as in 5:32, the reading of some manuscripts
the closing words are missing in a number of early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts give the exception in the words of 5:32 and say the husband "makes her commit adultery". Several early manuscripts lack the final clause, which may have been added from 5:32. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the exception applies to the whole case: divorce and remarriage
alternatives: the exception permits divorce but not remarriage
decisions.reason: The exception stands between "divorces" and "marries another", and most naturally governs both. Some read it as allowing a husband to separate from an unfaithful wife but not to marry again.

decisions.choice: I tell you: Jesus speaks on his own authority beside Moses
decisions.reason: As in the sayings of 5:21-48, Jesus sets his own word beside what the law allowed.

decisions.choice: inmoralidad sexual (L); infidelidad sexual (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the broad word, Balanced and Readable say what it means here, the wife's sexual unfaithfulness (meaning decision m1, uncertain). "Fornicación" now names sex between unmarried people and would narrow the sense.

decisions.choice: uasherati (L, B); kukosa uaminifu katika ndoa (R); anazini / ana hatia ya uzinzi
decisions.reason: The exception is a broad word for sexual sin, here the wife's unfaithfulness (meaning decision m1, uncertain); Literal and Balanced keep the broad "uasherati", and Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does. The verb that follows is the word for adultery, "kuzini".

decisions.choice: "gian dâm" (L); "vợ đã không chung thủy" (B, R) for porneia
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 5:32: the exception keeps its own word, apart from "ngoại tình" for adultery.

decisions.choice: "음행" (L); "성적으로 부정을 저지른" (B); "다른 남자와 성관계를 한" (R); "이혼당한 여자"
decisions.reason: The wording of the Korean Matthew 5:32, which states the same exception; the footnoted meaning decision says the wife's unfaithfulness is meant.

source.text: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Εἰ οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ αἰτία τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μετὰ τῆς γυναικός, οὐ συμφέρει γαμῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: Say to him the disciples, If thus is the case of the man with the wife, not it is better to marry.

en.L: The disciples say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If such is the case of the man with [his] wife, it is not better to marry."
en.B: His disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If that is how it stands between a man and his wife, then it would be better not to marry at all."
en.R: Jesus's followers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If a man cannot divorce his wife, it is better for him not to get married."

es.L: Le dicen los discípulos: «Si tal es la situación del hombre con [su] mujer, no conviene casarse».
es.B: Sus discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Si así están las cosas entre un hombre y su mujer, entonces más vale no casarse».
es.R: Los discípulos de Jesús {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Si un hombre no puede divorciarse de su esposa, es mejor que no se case».

fr.L: Les disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Si telle est la situation de l’homme avec [sa] femme, il n’est pas avantageux de se marier. »
fr.B: {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Si c’est ainsi que les choses se passent entre un homme et sa femme, mieux vaut ne pas se marier du tout ! »
fr.R: Les disciples de Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Si un homme ne peut pas divorcer d’avec sa femme, il vaut mieux qu’il ne se marie pas. »

sw.L: Wanafunzi wanamwambia, "Kama hivyo ndivyo ilivyo kati ya mwanamume na mke [wake], si bora kuoa."
sw.B: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimwambia, "Ikiwa ndivyo mambo yalivyo kati ya mume na mkewe, basi ni afadhali mtu asioe kabisa."
sw.R: Wanafunzi wa Yesu walimwambia, "Ikiwa mwanamume hawezi kumtaliki mkewe, ni afadhali asioe."

vi.L: Các môn đồ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Nếu sự thể giữa người chồng với vợ là như vậy, thì không nên cưới vợ."
vi.B: Các môn đồ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Nếu chuyện vợ chồng là như thế thì thà đừng lấy vợ còn hơn."
vi.R: Các môn đồ thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Nếu người đàn ông không được ly dị vợ mình, thì tốt hơn là đừng lấy vợ."

ko.L: 제자들이 그분께 말한다. "남자와 아내의 사정이 그러하다면, 결혼하는 것이 유익하지 않습니다."
ko.B: 제자들이 예수께 말했다. "남편과 아내 사이가 그런 것이라면, 차라리 결혼하지 않는 것이 낫겠습니다."
ko.R: 제자들이 예수께 말했다. "남자가 아내와 이혼할 수 없다면, 결혼하지 않는 편이 낫겠습니다."

decisions.choice: case: the situation, the terms on which a man is bound to his wife
decisions.reason: It is the same word as "cause" in 19:3. The Pharisees asked about a cause for divorce; the disciples now speak of the "case" of marriage itself.

decisions.choice: it is not better to marry: marriage seems too great a risk if it cannot be ended
decisions.reason: The disciples are taken aback by how strict Jesus is. Their remark leads to his words about those who do not marry.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: if a man cannot divorce his wife
alternatives: if such is the case of the man with his wife
decisions.reason: Readable says what "such" refers to.

decisions.choice: "thưa" (B, R) for the disciples speaking to Jesus
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks the disciples' respect in the verb, as in Mark 9:38 and 10:37; Literal keeps the plain "nói" of the historic present.

decisions.choice: "사정" for aitia; "결혼하는 것이 유익하지 않다" (L); present "말한다" (L)
decisions.reason: The case is the terms on which a man is bound to his wife (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Greek negative "it is not profitable to marry", Balanced and Readable say it is better not to marry.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ πάντες χωροῦσι τὸν λόγον τοῦτον ἀλλ’ οἷς δέδοται.

records.literal_gloss: He but said to them, Not all accept the word this but [those] to whom it has been given.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Not all [people] accept this word, but [only those] to whom it has been given.
en.B: He answered them, "This saying is not something everyone can accept. Only those to whom it has been given can do so.
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Not everyone can accept this teaching. Only the people God gives this gift to can accept it.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «No todos aceptan esta palabra, sino [solo] aquellos a quienes ha sido dado.
es.B: Él les respondió: «No todos pueden aceptar este dicho, sino solo aquellos a quienes se les ha concedido.
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «No todos pueden aceptar esta enseñanza. Solo pueden aceptarla aquellos a quienes Dios les da este don.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Tous ne reçoivent pas cette parole, mais [seulement] ceux à qui cela a été donné.
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Tout le monde ne peut pas accepter cette parole. Seuls le peuvent ceux à qui cela a été donné.
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Tout le monde ne peut pas accepter cet enseignement. Seuls ceux qui reçoivent ce don de Dieu peuvent l’accepter.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliwaambia, "Si wote wanaolipa nafasi neno hili, bali [ni wale tu] waliopewa.
sw.B: Aliwajibu, "Si kila mtu anaweza kulikubali neno hili. Ni wale tu waliopewa uwezo huo wanaoweza.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Si kila mtu anaweza kukubali fundisho hili. Ni wale tu ambao Mungu amewapa kipawa hiki wanaoweza kulikubali.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Không phải mọi người đều tiếp nhận được lời này, nhưng [chỉ] những người đã được ban cho.
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Không phải ai cũng chấp nhận được lời này, chỉ những người được ban cho mới chấp nhận được.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Không phải ai cũng có thể chấp nhận lời dạy này. Chỉ những người được Đức Chúa Trời ban cho ơn này mới chấp nhận được.

ko.L: 그러나 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "모든 사람이 이 말을 받아들이는 것은 아니다. 그것이 주어진 사람들만 [받아들인다].
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "이 말은 모든 사람이 받아들일 수 있는 것이 아니다. 그것을 받은 사람들만 받아들일 수 있다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "모든 사람이 이 가르침을 받아들일 수 있는 것은 아니다. 하나님께서 그런 은사를 주신 사람들만 받아들일 수 있다.

decisions.choice: this word: the disciples' saying that it is better not to marry
alternatives: Jesus's own teaching on divorce in 19:9
decisions.reason: What follows is about those who do not marry, so "this word" most likely points to the disciples' remark: not everyone can live unmarried. Others take it as Jesus's teaching on divorce, which only those given grace can keep.

decisions.choice: to whom it has been given: God gives the ability
decisions.reason: The passive points to God as the giver, as in 13:11.

decisions.choice: accept: make room for, take in and live by
decisions.reason: The verb means to have room for something. Here it means to receive a teaching and be able to live it.

decisions.choice: the people God gives this gift to
alternatives: those to whom it has been given
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver.

decisions.choice: wanaolipa nafasi (who make room for) (L); kukubali (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to make room for something, and so to take it in and live by it (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps that picture with "kulipa nafasi", as again in verse 12; Balanced and Readable say "accept", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "được Đức Chúa Trời ban cho ơn này" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable: the passive points to God as the giver.

decisions.choice: [받아들인다]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the verb to be understood in the second half; Literal brackets it. The passive "has been given" means God gives (meaning decision); Readable names him, as the English does.

source.text: εἰσὶν γὰρ εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ἐγεννήθησαν οὕτως, καὶ εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες εὐνουχίσθησαν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ εἰσὶν εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες εὐνούχισαν ἑαυτοὺς διὰ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: There are for eunuchs who from womb of mother were born thus, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by the men, and there are eunuchs who made eunuchs themselves for the sake of the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: For there are eunuchs who were born so from [their] mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by {{gender:people|men}}, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of the heavens.
en.B: For some are eunuchs because they were born that way; some have been made eunuchs by others; and some have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.
en.R: Some men are eunuchs: they cannot marry and have children. Some were born that way. Others were made that way by other people, who cut their bodies. And some choose to live like eunuchs and not marry, for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.

es.L: Porque hay eunucos que desde el seno de [su] madre nacieron así, y hay eunucos que fueron hechos eunucos por {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}, y hay eunucos que se convirtieron en eunucos ellos mismos a causa del reino de los cielos.
es.B: Unos son eunucos de nacimiento; a otros los hicieron eunucos los demás; y otros se han hecho eunucos ellos mismos por el reino de los cielos.
es.R: Algunos hombres son eunucos: no pueden casarse ni tener hijos. Unos nacieron así. A otros los dejaron así otras personas, mutilando su cuerpo. Y otros eligen vivir como eunucos y no casarse, por el reino de los cielos.

fr.L: Car il y a des eunuques qui sont nés ainsi du ventre de [leur] mère, et il y a des eunuques qui ont été faits eunuques par les {{gender:humains|hommes}}, et il y a des eunuques qui se sont faits eunuques eux-mêmes à cause du royaume des cieux.
fr.B: Car certains sont eunuques dès leur naissance ; d’autres ont été rendus eunuques par la main des autres ; d’autres enfin se sont faits eunuques eux-mêmes à cause du royaume des cieux.
fr.R: Certains hommes sont eunuques : ils ne peuvent pas se marier et avoir des enfants. Certains sont nés comme cela. D’autres sont devenus comme cela à cause d’autres gens, qui ont mutilé leur corps. Et d’autres choisissent de vivre comme des eunuques et de ne pas se marier, pour le royaume des cieux.

sw.L: Kwa kuwa kuna matowashi ambao walizaliwa hali hiyo tangu tumbo la mama [zao], na kuna matowashi ambao walihasiwa na watu, na kuna matowashi ambao walijihasi wenyewe kwa sababu ya ufalme wa mbinguni.
sw.B: Kwa maana wengine ni matowashi kwa sababu walizaliwa hivyo; wengine walihasiwa na watu; na wengine wamejiweka kuwa matowashi kwa ajili ya ufalme wa mbinguni.
sw.R: Wanaume wengine ni matowashi: hawawezi kuoa na kuzaa watoto. Wengine walizaliwa hivyo. Wengine walifanywa hivyo na watu wengine, waliowakata miili yao. Na wengine wanachagua kuishi kama matowashi bila kuoa, kwa ajili ya ufalme wa mbinguni.

vi.L: Vì có những người hoạn đã sinh ra như vậy từ lòng mẹ, có những người hoạn đã bị người ta hoạn, và có những người hoạn đã tự hoạn mình vì vương quốc thiên đàng.
vi.B: Vì có người là hoạn vì sinh ra đã như vậy; có người là hoạn vì bị người khác hoạn; và có người tự làm hoạn mình vì vương quốc thiên đàng.
vi.R: Có những người đàn ông không thể lấy vợ và có con. Có người sinh ra đã như vậy. Có người bị người khác thiến, nên phải như vậy. Và có người tự chọn sống như thế, không lấy vợ, vì vương quốc thiên đàng.

ko.L: 어머니의 태에서부터 그렇게 태어난 고자들이 있고, 사람들에 의해 고자가 된 고자들이 있고, 천국 때문에 스스로 고자가 된 고자들이 있기 때문이다.
ko.B: 어떤 사람은 날 때부터 고자이고, 어떤 사람은 다른 사람들이 고자로 만들었으며, 또 어떤 사람은 천국을 위해 스스로 고자가 되었다.
ko.R: 세상에는 고자들이 있다. 그들은 결혼해서 자녀를 낳을 수 없는 남자들이다. 어떤 사람은 날 때부터 그렇다. 어떤 사람은 다른 사람들이 몸을 상하게 해서 그렇게 되었다. 또 어떤 사람은 천국을 위해 스스로 결혼하지 않고 살기로 했다.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: men unable to father children, either from birth or by castration
decisions.reason: In the ancient world some men were castrated to serve in royal households (Acts 8:27). The law kept such men from the assembly (Deuteronomy 23:1), but God promised them a place among his people (Isaiah 56:3-5).

decisions.choice: made themselves eunuchs: chose not to marry
decisions.reason: The third kind is a picture. Jesus speaks of people who freely give up marriage, as the first two kinds could not marry. The law forbade cutting the body in this way (Deuteronomy 23:1), and Jesus does not command it.

decisions.choice: for the sake of the kingdom of heaven: to be free to serve God's kingdom
alternatives: in order to enter the kingdom
because they have been divorced and do not remarry
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means giving up marriage to give oneself to the work of the kingdom, as Paul says in 1 Corinthians 7:32-35. Some take it as the way a divorced disciple stays single (19:9), or as a condition for entering the kingdom.

decisions.choice: they cannot marry and have children; who cut their bodies; choose to live like eunuchs and not marry
alternatives: eunuchs; made eunuchs; made themselves eunuchs
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a eunuch is and what the third kind means.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: As the English Literal {{gender:people|men}}: the Greek word means human beings, and Spanish can say it either way. Balanced and Readable say "los demás" and "otras personas", which need no span.

decisions.choice: le royaume des cieux at every level (for 19:12-14)
decisions.reason: The term settled for the New Testament: the French plural "des cieux" is the familiar form and also keeps the Greek plural, so all three levels can share it.

decisions.choice: walihasiwa (were castrated) (L, B); walijihasi wenyewe (castrated themselves) (L); wamejiweka kuwa matowashi (B)
decisions.reason: Swahili has one verb, "kuhasi", for making a man a eunuch. Literal keeps the Greek verb for all three groups, as the English Literal does; the third group made themselves eunuchs in the sense of choosing not to marry (meaning decision m2), so Balanced says "set themselves to be eunuchs" and Readable says what it means. "Kujifanya" was avoided because it usually means "to pretend to be".

decisions.choice: "người hoạn", "hoạn" (L, B); a description with "thiến" (R) for eunuchs
decisions.reason: "hoạn quan" means a court official; the saying is about men who cannot or do not marry, so Literal and Balanced use the general "hoạn" and Readable explains, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "고자" for eunouchos; Readable says what it means and that the third kind chose not to marry
decisions.reason: Eunuchs are men unable to father children, from birth or by castration (meaning decision); "고자" is the plain Korean word for such a man, where "내시" is a court official. It can also be used as an insult, so a native reviewer should judge it.

decisions.choice: "사람들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" already includes men and women (style guide, section 7).

records.literal_gloss: The [one] being able to accept, let him accept.

en.L: The one who is able to accept [this], let {{gender:them|him}} accept [it]."
en.B: Let anyone who is able to accept this accept it."
en.R: If you are able to accept this teaching, then accept it."

es.L: El que pueda aceptar[lo], que [lo] acepte».
es.B: Quien sea capaz de aceptar esto, que lo acepte».
es.R: Si alguien puede aceptar esta enseñanza, que la acepte».

fr.L: Que celui qui peut accepter [cela] l’accepte. »
fr.B: Que celui qui est capable d’accepter cela l’accepte. »
fr.R: Si vous pouvez accepter cet enseignement, alors acceptez-le. »

sw.L: Yule awezaye kulipa nafasi, na alipe nafasi."
sw.B: Kila anayeweza kulikubali neno hili, na alikubali."
sw.R: Ikiwa unaweza kulikubali fundisho hili, basi likubali."

vi.L: Người nào có thể tiếp nhận [điều này], hãy tiếp nhận [điều ấy]."
vi.B: Ai có thể chấp nhận điều này thì hãy chấp nhận."
vi.R: Nếu các con có thể chấp nhận lời dạy này, thì hãy chấp nhận."

ko.B: 이 말을 받아들일 수 있는 사람은 받아들이도록 하여라."
ko.R: 이 가르침을 받아들일 수 있는 사람은 받아들여라."

decisions.choice: let him accept it: an invitation to those given the gift, not a command for all
alternatives: a rule that all disciples must stay unmarried
decisions.reason: The saying echoes 19:11. Remaining unmarried is for those able to receive it, as "whoever has ears" in 11:15.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The saying is for anyone able to accept it.

decisions.choice: If you are able ... then accept it
alternatives: The one who is able, let him accept
decisions.reason: Readable speaks directly to the hearer.

decisions.choice: Si alguien puede ... que la acepte
decisions.reason: The English Readable turns the saying to "you". In Spanish a "you" here would have to be singular or plural, and either would narrow it; "si alguien" keeps it open to anyone, as the Greek is (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "Que celui qui peut … l’accepte", with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs {{gender:them|him}}. French "celui qui" already means anyone, so the style guide puts no span on it. Readable speaks to the disciples with "vous", since Jesus is answering them (19:10-11).

decisions.choice: "받아들일 수 있는 사람은 받아들여라"; "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: An invitation to those given the gift (meaning decision); the third-person command becomes a plain imperative to "the one who can", which Korean needs no pronoun for.

source.text: Τότε προσηνέχθησαν αὐτῷ παιδία ἵνα τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιθῇ αὐτοῖς καὶ προσεύξηται· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμησαν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Then were brought to him little children that the hands he might lay on them and might pray; the but disciples rebuked them.

en.L: Then little children were brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might lay [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on them and pray; but the disciples rebuked them.
en.B: After this, some people brought young children to Jesus so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on them and pray for them. But the disciples spoke sternly to the people.
en.R: Then some people brought their little children to Jesus. They wanted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on the children and pray for them. But Jesus's followers told the people to stop.

es.L: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fueron traídos niños para que les impusiera las manos y orara; pero los discípulos los reprendieron.
es.B: Después de esto, algunas personas llevaron unos niños pequeños a Jesús para que les impusiera las manos y orara por ellos. Pero los discípulos reprendieron a esa gente.
es.R: Entonces algunas personas llevaron a sus niños pequeños a Jesús. Querían que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les pusiera las manos encima y orara por ellos. Pero los discípulos de Jesús les dijeron a esas personas que no lo hicieran.

fr.L: Alors on {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} amena de petits enfants pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur impose les mains et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prie ; mais les disciples les réprimandèrent.
fr.B: Après cela, des gens {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} amenèrent de jeunes enfants pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pose les mains sur eux et prie pour eux. Mais les disciples rabrouèrent ces gens.
fr.R: Ensuite, des gens ont amené leurs petits enfants à Jésus. Ils voulaient qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pose les mains sur les enfants et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prie pour eux. Mais les disciples de Jésus leur ont dit d’arrêter.

sw.L: Kisha watoto wadogo waliletwa {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} ili aweke mikono juu yao na kuomba; lakini wanafunzi wakawakemea.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo, watu fulani walimletea Yesu watoto wadogo ili aweke mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yao na kuwaombea. Lakini wanafunzi waliwakemea watu hao.
sw.R: Kisha watu fulani walimletea Yesu watoto wao wadogo. Walitaka aweke mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu ya watoto hao na kuwaombea. Lakini wanafunzi wa Yesu waliwaambia watu hao waache.

vi.L: Bấy giờ có người đem các trẻ nhỏ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt tay trên chúng và cầu nguyện; nhưng các môn đồ quở trách họ.
vi.B: Sau đó, người ta đem các em nhỏ đến với Đức Giê-xu để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt tay trên các em và cầu nguyện cho các em. Nhưng các môn đồ rầy la họ.
vi.R: Rồi có mấy người đem con nhỏ của mình đến với Đức Giê-xu. Họ muốn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt tay trên các em và cầu nguyện cho các em. Nhưng các môn đồ bảo họ đừng làm vậy.

ko.L: 그때에 [사람들이] 어린아이들을 그분께 데려왔다. 그분이 그들에게 손을 얹고 기도해 주시게 하려는 것이었다. 그러나 제자들이 그들을 꾸짖었다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 사람들이 어린아이들을 예수께 데려왔다. 예수께서 아이들에게 손을 얹고 기도해 주시기를 바랐던 것이다. 그런데 제자들이 그 사람들을 꾸짖었다.
ko.R: 그때 사람들이 자기 어린아이들을 예수께 데려왔다. 예수께서 아이들에게 손을 얹고 기도해 주시기를 바랐던 것이다. 그런데 제자들은 그 사람들에게 그러지 말라고 나무랐다.

decisions.choice: to lay hands on them and pray: to bless them
decisions.reason: Laying hands on someone with prayer was a way of blessing (Genesis 48:14). Parents wanted a blessing from a holy man for their children.

decisions.choice: rebuked them: those who brought the children
decisions.reason: "Them" most naturally means the people bringing the children, though it could include the children too. The disciples thought they were a bother.

decisions.choice: little children: young children
decisions.reason: The word is used of young children, as in 18:2-5.

decisions.choice: some people brought
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who brought them; the Greek is passive.

decisions.choice: las manos, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: English says "his hands" and marks the pronoun. Spanish uses the article for parts of the body ("les impusiera las manos"), so there is no possessive for the setting to capitalise. The same in verse 15.

decisions.choice: les disciples at Readable too (for the whole passage)
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers" because "disciples" is church language in English. French "disciple" is an everyday word, and Mark and Luke keep it at Readable (19:10 too).

decisions.choice: "các trẻ nhỏ" (L); "các em nhỏ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 10:13-16: "em" is the warm word for a young child in Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: [사람들이]
decisions.reason: The Greek passive "were brought" has no Korean equivalent that reads naturally; Literal names the unstated bringers in brackets.

decisions.choice: "꾸짖다" (L, B); "나무라다" (R); "그 사람들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Those rebuked are the ones who brought the children (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say so, as the Korean Mark 10:13 does.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτὰ ἐλθεῖν πρός με, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus said, Let the little children and not forbid them to come to me, of the for such is the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: But Jesus said, "Let the little children [be], and do not forbid them to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for the kingdom of the heavens belongs to such [as these]."
en.B: Jesus said, "Let the children be. Do not prevent them from coming to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because the kingdom of heaven is for those who are like them."
en.R: But Jesus said, "Let the little children come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Do not stop them! The kingdom of heaven belongs to people who are like these children."

es.L: Pero Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} a los niños, y no les {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}} venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque a los que son así pertenece el reino de los cielos».
es.B: Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} tranquilos a los niños. No les {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}} que vengan a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque el reino de los cielos es para los que son como ellos».
es.R: Pero Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} que los niños vengan a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. ¡No se lo {{plural_you:impidan|impidáis}}! El reino de los cielos es de los que son como estos niños».

fr.L: Mais Jésus dit : « Laissez les petits enfants, et ne les empêchez pas de venir à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, car le royaume des cieux est à leurs semblables. »
fr.B: Jésus dit : « Laissez faire les enfants. Ne les empêchez pas de venir à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, car le royaume des cieux est pour ceux qui leur ressemblent. »
fr.R: Mais Jésus a dit : « Laissez les petits enfants venir vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Ne les en empêchez pas ! Le royaume des cieux est à ceux qui sont comme ces enfants. »

sw.L: Lakini Yesu alisema, "Waacheni watoto wadogo, wala msiwazuie kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, kwa maana ufalme wa mbinguni ni wa walio kama hawa."
sw.B: Yesu alisema, "Waacheni watoto hao. Msiwazuie kuja {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, kwa sababu ufalme wa mbinguni ni kwa ajili ya wale walio kama wao."
sw.R: Lakini Yesu alisema, "Waruhusuni watoto wadogo waje {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}. Msiwazuie! Ufalme wa mbinguni ni mali ya watu walio kama watoto hawa."

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói: "Hãy để các trẻ nhỏ [yên], đừng ngăn cản chúng đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì vương quốc thiên đàng thuộc về những người như chúng."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Hãy để các em nhỏ yên. Đừng ngăn cản các em đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, vì vương quốc thiên đàng là dành cho những người giống như các em."
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nói: "Hãy để các em nhỏ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Đừng ngăn các em lại! Vương quốc thiên đàng thuộc về những người giống như các em này."

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "어린아이들을 [그대로] 두어라. 그리고 그들이 내게 오는 것을 막지 마라. 천국은 이런 사람들의 것이기 때문이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "어린아이들을 그냥 두어라. 그들이 내게 오는 것을 막지 마라. 천국은 이런 사람들의 것이다."
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "어린아이들이 내게 오게 해라. 막지 마라! 천국은 이 아이들과 같은 사람들의 것이다."

decisions.choice: of such is the kingdom: it belongs to children and to those who are like them
alternatives: it is made up of children
decisions.reason: "Such" means people of this kind. As in 18:3-4, the kingdom is received by those who, like children, are lowly and depend on others.

decisions.choice: let: leave them alone, allow them
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to forgive, to leave or to allow; here it means to let the children be.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos (every level)
decisions.reason: Matthew's name for God's kingdom, the term used for it throughout Matthew. The Spanish plural "los cielos" is natural in this phrase, so every level keeps it, where English changes to "heaven" at Balanced and Readable. The same in verse 12.

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni (every level)
decisions.reason: Matthew's name for God's kingdom, the term used for it throughout Matthew. "Mbinguni" (in heaven) is the natural Swahili form and stands for the Greek plural at every level. The same in verse 12.

decisions.choice: [그대로]
decisions.reason: "Let" here is "leave them alone" (meaning decision); Korean "두어라" needs an adverb to say it, which Literal brackets. "이런 사람들" covers the children and those like them.

source.text: καὶ ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἐπορεύθη ἐκεῖθεν.

records.literal_gloss: And having laid the hands on them he went from there.

en.L: And after laying [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands on them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on from there.
en.B: He put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on them, and then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on from there.
en.R: Jesus put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands on the children to bless them. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place.

es.L: Y después de imponerles las manos, se fue de allí.
es.B: Les impuso las manos, y luego se marchó de allí.
es.R: Jesús puso las manos sobre los niños para bendecirlos. Después se fue de aquel lugar.

fr.L: Et, leur ayant imposé les mains, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} partit de là.
fr.B: Il posa les mains sur eux, puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} poursuivit sa route.
fr.R: Jésus a posé les mains sur les enfants pour les bénir. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est parti de cet endroit.

sw.L: Na akiisha kuweka mikono juu yao, aliondoka hapo.
sw.B: Aliweka mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu yao, kisha akaondoka hapo.
sw.R: Yesu aliweka mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} juu ya watoto hao ili kuwabariki. Kisha akaondoka mahali hapo.

vi.L: Và sau khi đặt tay trên chúng, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời khỏi nơi đó.
vi.B: Ngài đặt tay trên các em, rồi rời khỏi nơi đó.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đặt tay trên các em để chúc phước cho các em. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rời khỏi nơi ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 그들에게 손을 얹으신 뒤에 거기에서 떠나가셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 아이들에게 손을 얹어 주시고, 그곳을 떠나셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 아이들에게 손을 얹고 복을 빌어 주셨다. 그리고 그곳을 떠나셨다.

decisions.choice: laying his hands on them: Jesus did what the parents asked
alternatives: a different act from the blessing asked for
decisions.reason: Matthew says simply that Jesus gave them the blessing the disciples had tried to prevent.

decisions.choice: to bless them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the laying on of hands meant (19:13).

decisions.choice: "복을 빌어 주셨다" (R)
decisions.reason: Laying on hands was to bless them (meaning decision); Readable says so, as the English Readable does. Korean needs no possessive for "his hands", so Literal has no bracket.
